nodes.label: Overhead Broiler House Frame (Siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:10)
nodes.description: Colour CCTV still shot near-vertically down onto the litter floor of a commercial broiler house. Several hundred mid-growth white birds are spread over a dusty grey floor at moderate density, with a horizontal blue feed pipe crossing the frame carrying five red-capped suspended pan feeders. On-screen text reads '1080P-IPC-Siren' (top left) and '2022-02-26 23:11:10' (top right). This is a sampled training/inspection frame for flock behaviour analysis, not a photograph of an individual bird.

nodes.label: Siren Camera Channel Label
nodes.description: The burned-in camera identifier '1080P-IPC-Siren' appearing in the upper-left of most frames. The suffix names an experimental stimulus/alarm condition rather than a location, so the channel name doubles as a per-frame condition label recoverable straight from the pixels.
nodes.rationale: Encoding the condition in the IP camera's display name means every exported frame is self-labelled even when the video files are renamed or re-cut, which removes the need for a separate side-car label file; the cost is that the label is permanently baked into the image region and becomes a spurious cue a model can latch onto.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.description: The fixed horizontal feed pipe and its row of five red-and-white circular pan feeders that bisect every frame at roughly the same image height. Because the camera is rigidly mounted, this line is a static spatial landmark that can serve as a reference for calibrating scale and for defining a feeding zone region-of-interest.
